intro.zh:
西班牙文有 27 個字母 —— 就是英文的 26 個再加一個 ñ。

這裡有個對你極為有利的消息：西班牙文的拼字與發音幾乎是一對一對應的。不像英文的 through / though / tough 各唸各的，西班牙文看到字就能唸出來，聽到音也大致拼得出來。與其記每個字的「長相」，不如記它的聲音。
intro.en:
Spanish has 27 letters — the same 26 as English plus ñ.

Here's something that works strongly in your favour: Spanish spelling and pronunciation line up almost one-to-one. Unlike English through / though / tough, a Spanish word tells you how to say it. Rather than memorising what a word looks like, learn what it sounds like.

rule.zh: 27 個字母，唯一比英文多的是 ñ。它不是「n 加符號」，而是獨立的一個字母，在字典裡排在 n 後面。
rule.en: There are 27 letters; the only one English doesn't have is ñ. It isn't "n with a mark" — it's a separate letter, filed after n in the dictionary.

note.zh: 注意：año（年）和 ano（肛門）是完全不同的兩個字
note.en: Careful: año (year) and ano (anus) are two completely different words.

rule.zh: 字母有自己的名字，拼名字或拼寫地址時會用到。母音的名字就是它的音：a、e、i、o、u。
rule.en: Letters have names, which you'll need when spelling out a name or an address. Vowel names are just their sounds: a, e, i, o, u.

rule.zh: ch、ll、rr 是雙字母組合，代表一個音，但 2010 年起不再算獨立字母。查字典時把它們當成兩個字母排序。
rule.en: ch, ll and rr are two-letter combinations that stand for one sound, but since 2010 they are no longer counted as separate letters. Alphabetise them as two letters.

pitfalls.zh:
西班牙文的拼字與發音幾乎一對一對應 —— 看到字就能唸，聽到音就能拼。

所以背單字的方式要對：不要盯著 restaurante 記它長什麼樣，而是出聲唸 res-tau-ran-te，讓耳朵和嘴巴記住它。

> 每學一個新字，先唸出聲三次再看意思。

另外有一件非做不可的事：**ñ 的波浪號不能省**。它是獨立字母，不是 n 的裝飾。

- ✗ Tengo treinta anos. → ✓ Tengo treinta **años**.

漏掉波浪號會讓句子的意思變得非常尷尬。打字前先確認輸入法打得出 ñ。
pitfalls.en:
Spanish spelling and pronunciation line up almost one-to-one — see the word, say the word; hear the word, spell the word.

So learn vocabulary the right way: don't stare at restaurante trying to memorise its shape. Say it out loud, res-tau-ran-te, and let your ears and mouth do the remembering.

> Say every new word out loud three times before you even look at the meaning.

One thing you must not skip: **the tilde on ñ is not optional**. It is its own letter, not a decorated n.

- ✗ Tengo treinta anos. → ✓ Tengo treinta **años**.

Without the tilde the sentence means something extremely awkward. Make sure your keyboard can actually produce ñ before you start typing.

title.zh: 母音與子音：五個純母音，以及不送氣的 p/t/k
title.en: Vowels and consonants: five pure vowels, and unaspirated p / t / k

intro.zh:
西班牙文只有 5 個母音，而且每個都「純」—— 從頭到尾不變化，不會滑動成雙母音。

真正需要練的是子音，其中最關鍵的一項是 p、t、k **不送氣**。這一點如果沒調整，你講的西班牙文會一直帶著很重的外國腔，即使文法全對。
intro.en:
Spanish has only 5 vowels, and each one is "pure" — it never changes or glides into a diphthong.

What actually needs practice is the consonants, and the single most important item is that p, t and k are **unaspirated**. If you don't adjust this, your Spanish will keep a heavy foreign accent even when your grammar is perfect.

rule.zh: 五個母音永遠只有一個唸法，不會因為位置而改變，也不會像英文那樣滑動成雙母音。
rule.en: Each of the five vowels has exactly one pronunciation. It never shifts with position and never glides into a diphthong the way English vowels do.

pitfalls.zh:
**這一課只有一個重點：p / t / k 不送氣。**

自我檢查法：手掌放在嘴前唸 papá。**如果感覺到一股氣噴到手掌，就是唸錯了。** 正確的唸法幾乎沒有氣流。同樣的測試也適用於 taxi 的 t 和 casa 的 c。

另外三件要留意的事：

- **b 和 v 完全同音**，都不咬下唇。
  - ✗ vivir 咬下唇唸成英文的 v
  - ✓ vivir 兩個 v 都唸成 b 的音
- **子音收尾的音節不要多加母音。**
  - ✗ el 唸成 e-le　✗ papel 唸成 pa-pe-le
  - ✓ el、papel 的結尾就停在子音上
- **沒有聲調。** 音高只用來表達語氣（疑問、驚訝），不改變字義。整句要平順流動，只在重音音節上稍微加強。

> 最難的是 rr 顫音，需要時間累積。先把 p/t/k 的送氣改掉 —— 那個改起來最快，對聽感的改善也最明顯。
pitfalls.en:
**This lesson has one priority: p / t / k without the puff of air.**

Self-check: hold your palm in front of your mouth and say papá. **If you feel a puff of air hit your hand, it's wrong.** The correct sound releases almost no air. The same test works for the t in taxi and the c in casa.

Three more things to watch:

- **b and v are exactly the same sound**, and neither touches the lower lip.
  - ✗ vivir with an English v, biting the lip
  - ✓ vivir with both v's pronounced like b
- **Don't add a vowel after a final consonant.**
  - ✗ el said as e-le　✗ papel said as pa-pe-le
  - ✓ el and papel simply stop on the consonant
- **There are no tones.** Pitch only carries intonation (a question, surprise); it never changes what a word means. Let the sentence flow evenly and only lean on the stressed syllable.

> The hardest sound is the rr trill, and it takes time. Fix the p/t/k aspiration first — it's the quickest change to make and the one that improves how you sound the most.

title.en: Stress rules and the written accent

intro.zh:
西班牙文沒有聲調，但有**重音** —— 每個字都有一個音節唸得比較重。

好消息是重音位置有規則可循，而且只有三條。學會這三條，你看到任何生字都知道該重讀哪裡；重音符號（´）出現的唯一理由，就是這個字不符合前兩條規則。
intro.en:
Spanish has no tones, but it does have **stress** — one syllable in every word is said with more force.

The good news is that stress follows rules, and there are only three of them. Learn those three and you'll know which syllable to stress in any word you've never seen. The written accent (´) exists for exactly one reason: to mark the words that break the first two rules.

rule.zh: 規則一：以**母音、n、s** 結尾的字，重音在**倒數第二個**音節。這類字最多，而且不用寫重音符號。
rule.en: Rule 1: words ending in a **vowel, n or s** are stressed on the **second-to-last** syllable. This covers the largest group, and they need no written accent.

rule.zh: 規則二：以**其他子音**（母音、n、s 以外）結尾的字，重音在**最後一個**音節，一樣不用寫符號。
rule.en: Rule 2: words ending in **any other consonant** are stressed on the **last** syllable — again with no written accent.

rule.zh: 規則三：不符合前兩條的，就**寫上重音符號**告訴你重音在哪。所以看到符號不是麻煩，是提示。
rule.en: Rule 3: anything that breaks the first two rules **carries a written accent** telling you where the stress falls. So the mark isn't a nuisance — it's a hint.

note.zh: 以母音結尾卻重讀最後一音節 → 要寫符號
note.en: Ends in a vowel but is stressed on the last syllable → needs the mark.

note.zh: 重音在倒數第三音節 → 一定要寫
note.en: Stressed on the third-to-last syllable → always written.

note.zh: 以 z 結尾卻重讀倒數第二音節 → 要寫
note.en: Ends in z but is stressed on the second-to-last syllable → needs the mark.

note.zh: 符號同時拆開 a 和 i，讓它們變成兩個音節 pa-ÍS
note.en: The mark also splits a and i into two syllables: pa-ÍS.

rule.zh: 重音符號也用來區分拼法相同、意思不同的字。這種用法跟音節位置無關。
rule.en: The written accent is also used to tell apart words spelled the same but meaning different things. This use has nothing to do with syllable position.

pitfalls.zh:
重音是「音量大、時間長」，不是「音調高」。整個字只有一個音節突出，其餘保持平穩。

兩個常見問題：

- **每個音節唸得一樣重** —— 聽起來很平板，母語者要多花力氣才聽得懂。
- **把重音唸成上揚的音調** —— 重音是加重，不是升調。

重音放錯會直接改變意思，這不是小事：

- 想說「爸爸」卻唸成 ✗ **PA**-pa（那是馬鈴薯） → ✓ pa-**PÁ**
- 想說「我說」卻唸成 ✗ ha-**BLÓ**（那是「他說了」，已經是不同時態） → ✓ **HA**-blo

寫的時候也一樣，符號少一個就是另一個字：

- ✗ Tengo un cafe. → ✓ Tengo un **café**.
- ✗ Tu eres mi amigo. → ✓ **Tú** eres mi amigo.（tu 是「你的」，tú 才是「你」）

> 學新字時連重音一起記。唸出聲並刻意把重音音節拉長一點，比在心裡默念有效得多。
pitfalls.en:
Stress means **louder and longer**, not higher in pitch. Exactly one syllable stands out; the rest stay even.

Two common problems:

- **Giving every syllable equal weight** — it sounds flat and takes listeners extra effort to follow.
- **Turning stress into a rising pitch** — stress is emphasis, not intonation.

Misplaced stress changes meaning outright, so this matters:

- meaning to say "dad" but saying ✗ **PA**-pa (that's a potato) → ✓ pa-**PÁ**
- meaning to say "I speak" but saying ✗ ha-**BLÓ** (that's "he spoke", already a different tense) → ✓ **HA**-blo

The same applies in writing — one missing mark makes it a different word:

- ✗ Tengo un cafe. → ✓ Tengo un **café**.
- ✗ Tu eres mi amigo. → ✓ **Tú** eres mi amigo. (tu means "your"; tú means "you")

> Learn each new word together with its stress. Saying it aloud and deliberately stretching the stressed syllable works far better than reading it silently.

title.zh: seseo 與 yeísmo：拉美發音的兩個關鍵
title.en: Seseo and yeísmo: the two keys to a Latin American accent

intro.zh:
這一課決定你聽起來像哪裡人。

網路上大量的西班牙文教材、YouTube 影片來自西班牙，那裡的 c、z 唸成類似英文 th 的 /θ/。**拉丁美洲沒有這個音。** 你的目標是厄瓜多，所以請從一開始就用拉美的唸法，不然之後要改掉很痛苦。
intro.en:
This lesson decides where you sound like you're from.

A great deal of the Spanish material online comes from Spain, where c and z are pronounced /θ/, like the th in think. **Latin America does not have that sound.** You're heading for Ecuador, so use the Latin American pronunciation from day one — it's painful to unlearn later.

rule.zh: **seseo**：c（在 e、i 前）和 z 一律唸 /s/，跟 s 完全同音。拉美不存在西班牙的 /θ/（th）音。
rule.en: **Seseo**: c (before e and i) and z are always /s/, identical to s. The /θ/ sound used in Spain does not exist in Latin America.

rule.zh: 結果是有些字聽起來完全一樣，只能靠上下文分辨。母語者也是這樣，不用擔心。
rule.en: As a result some words sound exactly alike and are told apart only by context. Native speakers do the same, so don't worry about it.

rule.zh: **yeísmo**：ll 和 y 唸成同一個音，接近國語「一」的聲母。
rule.en: **Yeísmo**: ll and y are pronounced as the same sound, close to the y in yes.

rule.zh: c 在 a、o、u 前面唸 /k/（不送氣），這跟 seseo 無關，別搞混。
rule.en: Before a, o and u, c is /k/ (unaspirated). That has nothing to do with seseo — don't mix the two up.

note.zh: 第一個 c 是 /s/，第二個 c 是 /k/ → SIN-ko
note.en: The first c is /s/, the second is /k/ → SIN-ko.

pitfalls.zh:
**不要學西班牙的 /θ/（類似英文 th 的音）。** 在厄瓜多，c（在 e、i 前）和 z 一律唸 /s/。

網路上大量教材來自西班牙，會把 gracias 唸成 GRA-thias。在厄瓜多這樣唸不會被誤解，但一聽就知道不是當地口音。從一開始就用 /s/，之後不必再改。

第二件事：**ll 不是兩個 l**。

- ✗ calle 唸成 CA-le
- ✓ calle 唸成 CA-ye

ll 和 y 是同一個音。ella 唸 E-ya，pollo 唸 PO-yo，llamar 唸 ya-MAR。

> seseo 的副作用：casa 和 caza 變成同音字，只能靠上下文分辨。這很正常，母語者也是這樣判斷的。
pitfalls.en:
**Don't learn Spain's /θ/ (the th sound).** In Ecuador, c (before e and i) and z are always /s/.

Plenty of online material comes from Spain and pronounces gracias as GRA-thias. In Ecuador that won't be misunderstood, but it immediately marks you as not local. Use /s/ from the start and you'll never have to change.

Second point: **ll is not two l's**.

- ✗ calle said as CA-le
- ✓ calle said as CA-ye

ll and y are the same sound. ella is E-ya, pollo is PO-yo, llamar is ya-MAR.

> A side effect of seseo: casa and caza become homophones, distinguishable only by context. That's completely normal — native speakers rely on context too.

note.zh: 拉美一律唸 s。不要唸成英文的 th。
note.en: Always /s/ in Latin America. Never the English th.

note.zh: 唸 k，而且不送氣，接近國語的ㄍ。
note.en: Pronounced /k/, and unaspirated — closer to an English g than to k.

note.zh: 接近國語「一」的聲母，兩者同音。
note.en: Close to the y in yes; the two spellings sound identical.

note.zh: seseo（無 /θ/）與 yeísmo（ll = y）是整個拉丁美洲的標準發音，厄瓜多含括在內。西班牙中北部才有 /θ/ 的區分。
note.en: Seseo (no /θ/) and yeísmo (ll = y) are standard across all of Latin America, Ecuador included. The /θ/ distinction exists only in central and northern Spain.

explain.zh: 拉美的 seseo 規則：c 在 e、i 前和 z 一律唸 /s/。gracias 唸 GRA-sias。西班牙的 GRA-thias 唸法在厄瓜多會顯得很突兀。
explain.en: The Latin American seseo rule: c before e or i, and z, are always /s/. gracias is GRA-sias. Spain's GRA-thias would sound out of place in Ecuador.

prompt.zh: 在厄瓜多，gracias 的 c 應該怎麼唸？

optionExplains.en: Correct. It's a direct result of seseo, and native speakers rely on context too.

intro.zh:
終於可以講整句話了。這一課給你三件事：打招呼、說出自己的名字、問對方的名字。

但這裡藏著一個決定：每次開口前，你都得先選 **tú** 還是 **usted**。這個選擇會改變動詞的形式，選錯不會被誤解，但會顯得失禮或過度生疏。在基多，這件事比多數教材講的還重要。
intro.en:
At last, whole sentences. This lesson gives you three things: how to greet someone, how to give your name, and how to ask for theirs.

But there's a decision hidden in here: before you open your mouth you have to pick **tú** or **usted**. That choice changes the form of the verb. Getting it wrong won't be misunderstood, but it will sound either rude or oddly distant. In Quito this matters more than most textbooks let on.

rule.zh: 依時間打招呼。注意都是複數形式（días、tardes、noches），這是固定用法。
rule.en: Greet according to the time of day. Note that all three are plural (días, tardes, noches) — that's fixed usage.

note.zh: 天黑後；見面和道別都能用
note.en: After dark; used both on arrival and on leaving.

note.zh: 任何時候都適用，最輕鬆
note.en: Works at any hour and is the most casual.

rule.zh: 說自己的名字，兩種都很常用。llamarse 是反身動詞，所以要帶 me / te / se。
rule.en: Two equally common ways to give your name. llamarse is reflexive, so it needs me / te / se.

rule.zh: 問對方名字 —— **這裡就要選 tú 或 usted 了**，動詞形式跟著變。
rule.en: Asking someone's name — **this is where you pick tú or usted**, and the verb follows.

note.zh: 對 usted：長輩、陌生人、正式場合
note.en: For usted: elders, strangers, formal settings.

rule.zh: 認識新朋友的標準回應。
rule.en: The standard replies when meeting someone new.

note.zh: 男生說 encantado，女生說 encantada
note.en: A man says encantado, a woman encantada.

rule.zh: 道別與道謝。
rule.en: Saying goodbye and saying thanks.

pitfalls.zh:
每次開口前都要先決定用 **tú** 還是 **usted**，因為這會改變動詞的形式：

- ¿Cómo **te llamas**?（tú）
- ¿Cómo **se llama** usted?（usted）

llamas 和 llama 長得不一樣，不能混用：

- ✗ ¿Cómo se llamas usted?　✗ ¿Cómo te llama?
- ✓ ¿Cómo **se llama** usted?　✓ ¿Cómo **te llamas**?

對陌生長輩用 tú 是最常見的失禮：

- ✗ ¿Cómo **estás**, señora? → ✓ ¿Cómo **está** usted, señora?

> **不確定就用 usted。** 對同輩用 usted 最多顯得正式一點；對長輩或陌生人用 tú 才是真的失禮。等對方說 "Puedes tutearme"（你可以用 tú 稱呼我）再換過去。

在基多所在的 Sierra 高地，usted 的使用範圍比多數教材說的更廣 —— 朋友之間、甚至家人之間都可能使用，並不代表關係疏遠。
pitfalls.en:
Before you speak you have to choose **tú** or **usted**, because it changes the verb form:

- ¿Cómo **te llamas**? (tú)
- ¿Cómo **se llama** usted? (usted)

llamas and llama are different forms and can't be mixed:

- ✗ ¿Cómo se llamas usted?　✗ ¿Cómo te llama?
- ✓ ¿Cómo **se llama** usted?　✓ ¿Cómo **te llamas**?

Using tú with an older stranger is the most common slip:

- ✗ ¿Cómo **estás**, señora? → ✓ ¿Cómo **está** usted, señora?

> **When in doubt, use usted.** With a peer, usted at worst sounds a bit formal; with an elder or a stranger, tú is genuinely impolite. Switch once they say "Puedes tutearme" (you can use tú with me).

In the Sierra highlands around Quito, usted is used far more widely than most textbooks suggest — between friends and even within families — and it doesn't signal distance.

note.zh: 基多所在的 Sierra 高地 usted 的使用範圍比多數教材預期得廣 —— 朋友之間、甚至父母與子女之間都可能用 usted，並不代表疏遠。厄瓜多不使用阿根廷式的 voseo（vos）。
note.en: In the Sierra highlands around Quito, usted covers far more ground than most textbooks suggest — between friends, and even between parents and children, without implying distance. Ecuador does not use Argentine-style voseo (vos).

explain.zh: 對陌生人或長輩一律用 usted：¿Cómo se llama usted? 在基多，禮貌等級用錯比文法錯誤更容易讓人不舒服，不確定時就選 usted。
explain.en: With strangers and elders, always use usted: ¿Cómo se llama usted? In Quito, getting the politeness level wrong causes more discomfort than a grammar slip, so pick usted when unsure.

prompt.zh: 你在市場遇到一位不認識的長者，該怎麼問她的名字？
prompt.en: You meet an older woman you don't know at the market. How do you ask her name?

optionExplains.zh: te llamas 是對 tú 用的，對陌生長輩太隨便。
optionExplains.en: te llamas is the tú form, too casual for an older stranger.

optionExplains.zh: 正確。對陌生人、長輩用 usted，動詞用第三人稱 se llama。
optionExplains.en: Correct. Strangers and elders take usted, with the third-person verb se llama.

optionExplains.zh: me llamo 是「我叫」，問自己沒有意義。
optionExplains.en: me llamo means "my name is" — no use for asking.

optionExplains.zh: llamarse 是反身動詞，一定要帶反身代名詞。
optionExplains.en: llamarse is reflexive and always needs its reflexive pronoun.

explain.zh: 這三句問候語都用複數，是固定用法，直接整組記起來就好：buenos días、buenas tardes、buenas noches。注意 días 是陽性所以配 buenos，tardes 和 noches 是陰性配 buenas。
explain.en: All three greetings are plural — fixed usage, so learn them as a set: buenos días, buenas tardes, buenas noches. Note días is masculine so it takes buenos, while tardes and noches are feminine and take buenas.

prompt.zh: 為什麼是 Buenos días 而不是 Bueno día？
prompt.en: Why is it Buenos días and not Bueno día?

options.zh: 因為這是固定的複數用法，問候語都用複數形式
options.en: Because these are fixed plural greetings

options.zh: 因為 bueno 永遠要加 s
options.en: Because bueno always takes an s

optionExplains.zh: día 是陽性（el día），但這不是關鍵。
optionExplains.en: día is masculine (el día), but that's not the point here.

optionExplains.zh: 正確。buenos días / buenas tardes / buenas noches 都是固定的複數問候語。
optionExplains.en: Correct. buenos días / buenas tardes / buenas noches are all fixed plural greetings.

optionExplains.zh: bueno 在其他地方不加 s，例如 un libro bueno。
optionExplains.en: bueno doesn't take an s elsewhere, e.g. un libro bueno.

optionExplains.zh: Bueno día 是錯的，母語者不會這樣說。
optionExplains.en: Bueno día is wrong; native speakers don't say it.

explain.zh: Me llamo Ana 或 Soy Ana 都對。llamarse 是反身動詞，「我」對應的反身代名詞是 me。
explain.en: Me llamo Ana or Soy Ana both work. llamarse is reflexive, and the pronoun for "I" is me.

prompt.en: My name is Ana.

explain.zh: 出身用 ser + de。主詞 yo 可以省略，因為 soy 已經表明是第一人稱。
explain.en: Origin uses ser + de. The subject yo can be dropped, since soy already marks the first person.

prompt.en: I'm from Taiwan.

explain.zh: 疑問詞 cómo 放句首，接著是反身代名詞 se、動詞 llama，最後才是主詞 usted。西班牙文的疑問句主詞常放在動詞後面。
explain.en: The question word cómo comes first, then the reflexive pronoun se and the verb llama, with the subject usted last. Spanish questions often put the subject after the verb.

prompt.en: What is your name, please?

explain.zh: Mucho gusto 是固定說法，不要拆開理解。後面接 me llamo + 名字。
explain.en: Mucho gusto is a set phrase — don't try to take it apart. It's followed by me llamo plus your name.

prompt.en: Nice to meet you, my name is Carlos.

explain.zh: 這是最安全的開場：時間問候 + usted 敬語。注意 está 的重音在最後一個音節。
explain.en: This is the safest opener: a time-of-day greeting plus the usted form. Note that está is stressed on the last syllable.

explain.zh: 多數教材會說「usted 用於正式場合」，但在厄瓜多 Sierra 高地，usted 的使用範圍廣得多 —— 朋友、甚至父母子女之間都可能用，並不代表關係疏遠。這是需要當地經驗才會知道的細節。
explain.en: Most textbooks say usted is for formal situations, but in the Ecuadorian Sierra its range is much wider — friends, and even parents and children, may use it without any sense of distance. This is the kind of detail you only learn locally.

prompt.zh: 在基多，朋友之間用 usted 稱呼對方，代表什麼？
prompt.en: In Quito, what does it mean when friends address each other as usted?

options.zh: 在 Sierra 高地這很常見，不代表疏遠
options.en: It's common in the Sierra highlands and doesn't imply distance

options.zh: 代表其中一方是外國人
options.en: That one of them is a foreigner

optionExplains.zh: usted 在當地不帶負面意味。
optionExplains.en: usted carries no negative connotation there.

optionExplains.zh: 正確。基多所在的高地區 usted 使用範圍比多數教材預期得廣，朋友甚至家人之間都可能使用。
optionExplains.en: Correct. In the highlands usted covers far more ground than most textbooks suggest, including friends and family.

optionExplains.zh: 當地人之間也這樣用。
optionExplains.en: Locals use it with each other too.

optionExplains.zh: 完全合乎文法。
optionExplains.en: It's perfectly grammatical.

explain.en: Mucho gusto is the standard reply on meeting someone, literally "much pleasure".

explain.zh: De nada 字面是「沒什麼」，就是中文的「不客氣」。
explain.en: De nada literally means "of nothing" — the standard reply to thanks.

intro.zh:
數字在旅途上用得比你想像的多：買東西、講價錢、說年齡、報房號、聽公車號碼。

好消息是你只要記住 0–15 這 16 個字，其餘幾乎都是照規律拼出來的。只有一個小陷阱：16 到 29 要合寫成一個字。
intro.en:
Numbers come up more than you'd expect on a trip: buying things, talking prices, giving your age, reading a room number, catching a bus number.

The good news is that you only have to memorise the 16 words from 0 to 15; nearly everything else is built from a pattern. There's just one catch: 16 through 29 are written as a single word.

rule.zh: 0–15 必須個別記住，沒有規律可循。
rule.en: 0–15 have to be memorised individually; there's no pattern.

examples.es: cero, uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco

rule.zh: 16–19 合寫成一個字：dieci + 個位數。注意 dieciséis 有重音符號。
rule.en: 16–19 are written as one word: dieci + the units digit. Note the accent on dieciséis.

note.zh: diez + y + seis 合起來寫，要加重音符號
note.en: diez + y + seis written together, and it takes an accent.

rule.zh: 21–29 也是合寫：veinti + 個位數。veintiuno、veintidós、veintitrés 有重音符號。
rule.en: 21–29 are also written as one word: veinti + the units digit. veintiuno, veintidós and veintitrés carry accents.

rule.zh: 31 以上就**分開寫**，中間加 y。這是最常搞混的分界點：29 以下合寫，31 以上分開。
rule.en: From 31 up the numbers are **written separately**, joined by y. This is the boundary people mix up: one word up to 29, separate words from 31.

rule.zh: uno 放在陽性名詞前面要縮成 un；陰性則變 una。
rule.en: Before a masculine noun uno shortens to un; the feminine form is una.

note.zh: 組合數字裡也一樣要縮
note.en: The shortening applies inside compound numbers too.

rule.zh: 說年齡用 tener（有），不是 ser。這是固定搭配。
rule.en: Age uses tener (to have), not ser. This pairing is fixed.

gloss.en: My dad is forty years old.

pitfalls.zh:
三件會出錯的事。

**一、16–29 合寫成一個字，31 以上分開寫。**

- ✓ dieciséis、veintidós、veinticinco（一個字，有些帶重音符號）
- ✓ treinta y uno、cuarenta y cinco（三個字，中間有 y）
- ✗ diez y seis　✗ cuarentaycinco

**二、年齡用 tener，不用 ser。**

- ✗ Soy treinta años. → ✓ **Tengo** treinta años.
- 問別人也一樣：¿Cuántos años **tiene** usted?

**三、uno 放在名詞前要縮短。**

- ✗ Tengo uno hermano. → ✓ Tengo **un** hermano.
- 陰性用 una：**una** hermana
- 組合數字裡也一樣：treinta y **un** años

> 這三項各自獨立，但都很常出現在同一句話裡：Tengo veintiún años. —— 縮短、合寫、tener 三者同時到齊。
pitfalls.en:
Three things go wrong here.

**1. 16–29 are written as one word; 31 and up are written separately.**

- ✓ dieciséis, veintidós, veinticinco (one word, some with an accent)
- ✓ treinta y uno, cuarenta y cinco (three words, joined by y)
- ✗ diez y seis　✗ cuarentaycinco

**2. Age uses tener, not ser.**

- ✗ Soy treinta años. → ✓ **Tengo** treinta años.
- Asking works the same way: ¿Cuántos años **tiene** usted?

**3. uno shortens before a noun.**

- ✗ Tengo uno hermano. → ✓ Tengo **un** hermano.
- Feminine takes una: **una** hermana
- The same applies inside compound numbers: treinta y **un** años

> These three are independent, but they often land in the same sentence: Tengo veintiún años. — shortening, one-word spelling and tener all at once.

explain.zh: 16–19 合寫成 dieci + 個位數。dieciséis 因為重音落在最後一個音節而以 s 結尾，所以要寫重音符號。
explain.en: 16–19 are written as dieci + the units digit. dieciséis takes an accent because the stress falls on the last syllable and it ends in s.

optionExplains.en: Correct. One word, with an accent.

optionExplains.en: No such form exists.

explain.zh: 分界點要記牢：16–29 合寫成一個字（dieciséis、veinticinco），31 以上分開寫加 y（cuarenta y cinco）。
explain.en: Remember the boundary: 16–29 are one word (dieciséis, veinticinco), 31 and up are written separately with y (cuarenta y cinco).

optionExplains.en: Correct. From 31 up it's always tens + y + units, written separately.

optionExplains.zh: 這是 21–29 的合寫模式，不適用於 40 以上。
optionExplains.en: That's the 21–29 one-word pattern, which doesn't apply above 40.

optionExplains.zh: 中間少了 y。
optionExplains.en: The y is missing.

explain.zh: 年齡固定用 tener：Tengo treinta años。西班牙文把年齡看成「擁有的年數」，所以不能用 ser。
explain.en: Age always uses tener: Tengo treinta años. Spanish treats age as a number of years you possess, so ser doesn't work here.

prompt.en: How do you say "I'm thirty years old"?

optionExplains.zh: 西班牙文不用 ser 表示年齡。
optionExplains.en: Spanish doesn't express age with ser.

optionExplains.zh: 正確。年齡用 tener（有），字面是「我有三十年」。
optionExplains.en: Correct. Age uses tener — literally "I have thirty years".

optionExplains.zh: estar 用於狀態和位置，不用於年齡。
optionExplains.en: estar is for states and locations, not age.

optionExplains.zh: hay 表示存在，跟年齡無關。
optionExplains.en: hay expresses existence and has nothing to do with age.

explain.zh: uno 放在陽性名詞前縮短成 un（un hermano），陰性則用 una（una hermana）。這個縮短在組合數字裡也一樣：treinta y un años。
explain.en: uno shortens to un before a masculine noun (un hermano); the feminine is una (una hermana). The same shortening applies inside compound numbers: treinta y un años.

optionExplains.en: hermana is feminine and takes una.

explain.en: Age uses tener, third person tiene. Note that neither the accent on papá nor the ñ in años can be dropped.

explain.en: This is the single most useful phrase for shopping — learn it whole. Note that Spanish questions take marks at both ends: ¿…?

explain.en: Ecuador has used the US dollar as its official currency since 2000, so prices are quoted in dólares. The c in quince is /s/ (seseo).

explain.en: veintitrés is written as one word, with an accent because the stress falls on the last syllable. Age uses tiene, the third-person form of tener.

explain.en: siete = 7. Note that this sentence uses tener for "has" — the same verb used for age.

prompt.zh: 一週有幾天？用西班牙文回答。
prompt.en: How many days are there in a week? Answer in Spanish.

optionExplains.en: seis is six.

optionExplains.zh: 正確。siete 是七。
optionExplains.en: Correct. siete is seven.

optionExplains.en: ocho is eight.

optionExplains.en: cinco is five.

explain.en: cuánto is the question word "how much"; as a question word it always carries a written accent.

intro.zh:
每一個西班牙文名詞都有性別 —— 不只是人和動物，桌子、書、城市、問題全都有。

先講一件能省你很多力氣的事：**不要問為什麼**。桌子為什麼是陰性？沒有原因，不是因為桌子比較柔美，也不是因為古人怎麼想。這純粹是語法上的分類，跟意義無關。接受這一點，學習速度會快很多。
intro.en:
Every Spanish noun has a gender — not just people and animals, but tables, books, cities and problems too.

Something that will save you a lot of effort: **don't ask why**. Why is a table feminine? There is no reason. It isn't because tables are somehow delicate. It's a purely grammatical classification with no connection to meaning. Accept that and you'll learn much faster.

rule.zh: 大原則：-o 結尾多半是陽性，-a 結尾多半是陰性。這條規則涵蓋約八成的名詞。
rule.en: The broad rule: words ending in -o are usually masculine, words ending in -a usually feminine. This covers about eighty percent of nouns.

rule.zh: 必背的例外。這些字違反上面的規則，只能個別記住。
rule.en: Exceptions worth memorising. These break the rule above and simply have to be learned one by one.

note.zh: 源自希臘文的 -ma 結尾字多為陽性
note.en: Nouns of Greek origin ending in -ma are usually masculine.

rule.zh: 其他字尾的規律：-ción、-sión、-dad、-tad 結尾一律陰性；-or 結尾多半陽性。
rule.en: Other reliable endings: -ción, -sión, -dad and -tad are always feminine; -or is usually masculine.

rule.zh: 指人的名詞通常隨真實性別變化字尾。有些字陰陽同形，只靠冠詞分辨。
rule.en: Nouns for people usually change their ending to match the person's gender. Some have one form for both and rely on the article alone.

note.en: The ending doesn't change — only the article does.

pitfalls.zh:
**性別無法從字義推測。** mesa 是陰性、libro 是陽性，這跟桌子或書本身的性質無關，純粹是語法分類。不要花時間找理由，那不存在。

之所以非記不可，是因為性別會牽動一整串：

- ✗ **el** mesa → ✓ **la** mesa
- ✗ la mesa **blanco** → ✓ la mesa **blanca**
- ✗ **los** mesas blancas → ✓ **las** mesas **blancas**

> **背單字時一定連冠詞一起背。背 la mesa，不要背 mesa。** 多花的力氣接近零，但省下的是之後每句話都要停下來猜性別的時間。

大原則是 -o 陽性、-a 陰性，涵蓋約八成。必背的例外只有幾個：

- ✗ la día、la problema、la mapa → ✓ **el** día、**el** problema、**el** mapa
- ✗ el mano → ✓ **la** mano

另外 -dad / -tad / -ción / -sión 結尾**一律陰性**，這條完全沒有例外，記起來很划算。
pitfalls.en:
**Gender cannot be worked out from meaning.** mesa is feminine and libro is masculine, and that has nothing to do with tables or books themselves — it's a grammatical class. Don't hunt for a reason; there isn't one.

It has to be learned because gender pulls a whole chain along with it:

- ✗ **el** mesa → ✓ **la** mesa
- ✗ la mesa **blanco** → ✓ la mesa **blanca**
- ✗ **los** mesas blancas → ✓ **las** mesas **blancas**

> **Always learn a noun together with its article. Learn la mesa, not mesa.** The extra effort is close to zero, and it saves you from stopping to guess the gender in every sentence you build.

The broad rule is -o masculine, -a feminine, which covers about eighty percent. There are only a handful of exceptions worth memorising:

- ✗ la día, la problema, la mapa → ✓ **el** día, **el** problema, **el** mapa
- ✗ el mano → ✓ **la** mano

Nouns ending in -dad / -tad / -ción / -sión are **always feminine** — a rule with no exceptions at all, so it's excellent value.

explain.en: These all follow the broad -o masculine / -a feminine pattern, so start by building the reflex on the easy cases.

intro.zh:
這一課要學的是一個概念，而不是一組新單字。

西班牙文有兩套冠詞：**定冠詞**（el / la）用在雙方都知道是哪一個的東西上，**不定冠詞**（un / una）用在第一次提到、或不特指哪一個的時候。難的不是記這四個字，而是判斷「什麼時候該用、什麼時候不該用」。
intro.en:
This lesson is about a concept rather than a set of new words.

Spanish has two sets of articles: the **definite** ones (el / la) for something both speakers already have in mind, and the **indefinite** ones (un / una) for something mentioned for the first time, or not any particular one. The hard part isn't memorising the four words — it's judging when to use one and when to leave it out.

rule.zh: 定冠詞：指特定的、雙方都知道的那一個。相當於中文的「那個」「這個」，但西班牙文用得頻繁得多。
rule.en: Definite articles point at a specific one that both speakers already have in mind. Spanish uses them far more often than you might expect.

examples.es: El libro está en la mesa.

note.zh: 雙方都知道是哪本書、哪張桌子

rule.zh: 不定冠詞：第一次提到，或不特指是哪一個。相當於中文的「一個」「某個」。
rule.en: Indefinite articles introduce something for the first time, or don't single one out.

rule.zh: **陰性名詞若以重音的 a- 開頭，單數要配 el**，純粹是為了避免兩個 a 連在一起難唸。名詞本身仍是陰性。
rule.en: **A feminine noun beginning with a stressed a- takes el in the singular**, purely to avoid two a sounds running together. The noun stays feminine.

pitfalls.zh:
錯誤集中在兩個方向。

**一、具體名詞前面漏掉冠詞。**

- ✗ Libro está en mesa. → ✓ **El** libro está en **la** mesa.
- ✗ Teléfono está aquí. → ✓ **El** teléfono está aquí.

只要是特定的、雙方都知道的東西，前面幾乎一定有冠詞。

**二、職業前面多加了冠詞。**

- ✗ Soy **un** estudiante. → ✓ Soy estudiante.
- ✗ Ella es **una** profesora. → ✓ Ella es profesora.

ser + 職業／國籍，不加冠詞。

> 自我檢查：造完句子後把每個名詞掃一遍，問「這個名詞前面有沒有東西？」除了職業、國籍這類例外，答案通常應該是「有」。

還有一個容易漏的：談論**整類事物**時要加定冠詞。

- ✓ Me gusta **el** café.（喜歡咖啡這種東西）
- ✓ **La** fruta es buena.（水果是好的）

初學階段寧可多加也不要漏加 —— 漏掉冠詞聽起來像電報，加錯只是小瑕疵。
pitfalls.en:
Mistakes cluster in two directions.

**1. Leaving out the article before a concrete noun.**

- ✗ Libro está en mesa. → ✓ **El** libro está en **la** mesa.
- ✗ Teléfono está aquí. → ✓ **El** teléfono está aquí.

If a noun is specific and both speakers know which one, it almost always has an article in front of it.

**2. Adding an article before a profession.**

- ✗ Soy **un** estudiante. → ✓ Soy estudiante.
- ✗ Ella es **una** profesora. → ✓ Ella es profesora.

ser + profession or nationality takes no article.

> Self-check: once a sentence is built, scan every noun and ask "is there anything in front of this?" Apart from professions and nationalities, the answer should usually be yes.

One more that's easy to miss: talking about a **whole category** takes the definite article.

- ✓ Me gusta **el** café. (coffee as a thing)
- ✓ **La** fruta es buena. (fruit in general)

Early on, prefer adding one to leaving one out — a missing article sounds like a telegram, while a wrong one is a minor blemish.

intro.zh:
複數規則本身很單純，兩三條就講完。真正需要適應的是：**複數會傳染** —— 冠詞、名詞、形容詞必須全部一起變。

los libros nuevos 三個字全都帶了 s，少任何一個都是錯的。
intro.en:
The plural rules themselves are simple — two or three lines cover them. What takes adjusting to is that **the plural spreads**: the article, the noun and the adjective all have to change together.

los libros nuevos carries an s on all three words, and dropping any one of them is an error.

rule.zh: 母音結尾 → 加 -s。
rule.en: Ends in a vowel → add -s.

rule.zh: 子音結尾 → 加 -es。
rule.en: Ends in a consonant → add -es.

rule.zh: -z 結尾 → 改成 -ces。因為 z 後面不能接 e，拼寫要跟著調整。
rule.en: Ends in -z → change to -ces, because z can't be followed by e, so the spelling adjusts.

note.zh: 重音符號**保留**：lá-pi-ces 的重音落在倒數第三音節，這類字一律要標符號
note.en: The accent is **kept**: lá-pi-ces is stressed on the third-from-last syllable, which always takes a mark.

rule.zh: 冠詞跟著變：el → los，la → las，un → unos，una → unas。
rule.en: The article changes too: el → los, la → las, un → unos, una → unas.

rule.zh: 形容詞也要跟著變複數，規則跟名詞一樣。
rule.en: Adjectives take the plural as well, following the same rules as nouns.

pitfalls.zh:
**複數會傳染。** 冠詞、名詞、形容詞必須同時變，漏掉任何一個都是錯的。

- ✗ las casa blanca
- ✗ las casas blanca
- ✓ **las casas blancas**

規則本身很單純：

- 母音結尾 → 加 **-s**：libro → libros
- 子音結尾 → 加 **-es**：ciudad → ciudades
- **-z 結尾 → 改成 -ces**：luz → luces、lápiz → lápices

> 自我檢查：決定用複數之後，把整串掃過去 —— 冠詞、名詞、形容詞，一個都不能漏。

lápiz → lápices 要特別注意：z 變成 c，而**重音符號保留**（lá-pi-ces 的重音落在倒數第三音節，這類字一律要標）。反過來 inglés → ingleses 的符號會消失，因為複數之後重音變成倒數第二音節又以 s 結尾，正好符合基本規則。
pitfalls.en:
**The plural spreads.** The article, the noun and the adjective all have to change together; missing any one of them is wrong.

- ✗ las casa blanca
- ✗ las casas blanca
- ✓ **las casas blancas**

The rules themselves are simple:

- ends in a vowel → add **-s**: libro → libros
- ends in a consonant → add **-es**: ciudad → ciudades
- **ends in -z → change to -ces**: luz → luces, lápiz → lápices

> Self-check: once you've decided on a plural, sweep across the whole phrase — article, noun, adjective, none of them optional.

lápiz → lápices deserves attention: the z becomes c, and **the accent is kept** (lá-pi-ces is stressed on the third-from-last syllable, which always takes a mark). The opposite happens with inglés → ingleses, where the mark disappears because the plural is stressed on the second-to-last syllable and ends in s, matching the basic rule.

title.zh: 主詞代名詞：五個人稱，沒有 vosotros
title.en: Subject pronouns: five persons, no vosotros

intro.zh:
這一課要建立一個核心概念：**動詞會隨主詞改變形狀**。ser 有五種長相，hablar 也有五種，每一種對應一個人稱。

同時要把一件事講清楚並記牢：本課程教的是拉丁美洲西班牙文，所以人稱只有 **5 個**，不是課本上常見的 6 個。西班牙的 vosotros 在拉美完全不使用，我們從頭到尾都不會教它 —— 這會替你省下不少力氣。
intro.en:
This lesson builds a core idea: **verbs change shape according to their subject**. ser has five forms, hablar has five forms, one for each person.

There's also something to make clear and remember: this course teaches Latin American Spanish, so there are only **5** persons, not the 6 you'll see in most textbooks. Spain's vosotros is not used in Latin America and we never teach it — which saves you a fair bit of effort.

rule.zh: 拉美西班牙文的五個主詞人稱。第二人稱複數一律用 ustedes。
rule.en: The five subject persons of Latin American Spanish. The second-person plural is always ustedes.

note.zh: 三者共用同一組動詞變化
note.en: All three share one set of verb forms.

note.zh: 同樣共用一組動詞變化
note.en: These also share one set of forms.

rule.zh: **不使用 vosotros。** 西班牙用 vosotros 表示「你們（親近）」，拉美一律用 ustedes，不分親疏。
rule.en: **vosotros is not used.** Spain uses vosotros for an informal "you all"; Latin America uses ustedes for everyone, formal or not.

note.en: You would never say vosotros habláis.

rule.zh: **厄瓜多不使用 voseo。** 阿根廷、烏拉圭等地用 vos 取代 tú，厄瓜多不是這樣，用 tú 就對了。
rule.en: **Ecuador does not use voseo.** Argentina and Uruguay replace tú with vos; Ecuador does not, so tú is correct.

rule.zh: usted 雖然意思是「您」，動詞卻用**第三人稱**形式，跟 él / ella 完全一樣。這是最容易搞混的一點。
rule.en: Although usted means "you", it takes **third-person** verb forms, exactly like él / ella. This is the easiest point to get wrong.

note.zh: 動詞同樣是 es，不是 eres
note.en: The verb is still es, not eres.

rule.zh: 主詞代名詞**通常省略**，因為動詞形式已經指明了人稱。只有在強調或避免混淆時才說出來。
rule.en: Subject pronouns are **usually omitted**, because the verb form already identifies the person. They appear only for emphasis or to avoid ambiguity.

note.en: No need to say Yo soy.

examples.es: Yo soy de Taiwán y él es de Ecuador.

gloss.zh: 我來自台灣，而他來自厄瓜多。
gloss.en: I'm from Taiwan and he's from Ecuador.

note.zh: 對比時才把代名詞說出來
note.en: The pronouns appear because the sentence is drawing a contrast.

pitfalls.zh:
三件事要同時建立。

**一、學動詞是學一整組，不是學一個字。**

看到 ser 就要想到五個形式：soy / eres / es / somos / son。只記住 ser 本身等於什麼都沒記住。

**二、主詞代名詞通常要省略。**

- ✓ Soy de Taiwán.（自然）
- ○ Yo soy de Taiwán.（文法正確，但聽起來像在強調「是我，不是別人」）

動詞形式已經帶了人稱資訊，代名詞只在強調或對比時才出現：Yo soy de Taiwán y **él** es de Ecuador.

**三、usted 用第三人稱動詞。**

- ✗ Usted **eres** profesor. → ✓ Usted **es** profesor.
- ✗ ¿Usted **tienes** hijos? → ✓ ¿Usted **tiene** hijos?

usted 的意思是「您」，動詞卻跟 él / ella 完全一樣。這是最常見的錯配。

> 好消息：本課程不教 vosotros（拉美不使用），所以你要記的變化比西班牙的教材少六分之一。
pitfalls.en:
Three things to build at once.

**1. Learning a verb means learning a whole set, not one word.**

When you see ser you need to think of all five forms: soy / eres / es / somos / son. Remembering ser by itself is remembering nothing.

**2. Subject pronouns are usually left out.**

- ✓ Soy de Taiwán. (natural)
- ○ Yo soy de Taiwán. (grammatical, but it sounds like you're stressing "*I* am, not someone else")

The verb form already carries the person, so the pronoun only appears for emphasis or contrast: Yo soy de Taiwán y **él** es de Ecuador.

**3. usted takes third-person verbs.**

- ✗ Usted **eres** profesor. → ✓ Usted **es** profesor.
- ✗ ¿Usted **tienes** hijos? → ✓ ¿Usted **tiene** hijos?

usted means "you", but its verb behaves exactly like él / ella. This is the most common mismatch.

> Good news: this course doesn't teach vosotros (unused in Latin America), so you have one sixth fewer forms to memorise than a textbook from Spain would give you.

note.zh: 拉丁美洲全境以 ustedes 作為唯一的第二人稱複數，不使用 vosotros。厄瓜多使用 tú／usted，不使用阿根廷式的 voseo（vos）。
note.en: Across all of Latin America, ustedes is the only second-person plural; vosotros is not used. Ecuador uses tú and usted, not Argentine-style voseo (vos).

explain.zh: 拉丁美洲的第二人稱複數只有 ustedes 一種。看到教材教 vosotros 可以直接跳過 —— 在厄瓜多用不到，還會顯得很奇怪。
explain.en: Latin America has only one second-person plural: ustedes. When a course teaches vosotros you can skip it — it's unused in Ecuador and would sound strange there.

optionExplains.en: Correct. Latin America always uses ustedes, formal or not.

optionExplains.en: No such form exists.

optionExplains.en: Correct. usted means "you", but the verb is the third-person es.

optionExplains.zh: soy 是「我」的形式。
optionExplains.en: soy is the "I" form.

optionExplains.zh: ustedes 是複數，動詞要用 son。
optionExplains.en: ustedes is plural and takes son.

explain.zh: ser 的第一人稱單數是 soy。ser 是完全不規則動詞，五個形式都要個別記：soy / eres / es / somos / son。
explain.en: The first-person singular of ser is soy. ser is completely irregular, so all five forms have to be memorised individually: soy / eres / es / somos / son.

explain.zh: ellos / ellas / ustedes 共用 son。記住這一格同時涵蓋「他們」和「你們」——因為拉美不用 vosotros。
explain.en: ellos / ellas / ustedes all share son. Remember this one slot covers both "they" and "you all" — because Latin America doesn't use vosotros.

explain.zh: hablar 是規則的 -ar 動詞，nosotros 形式是字根 habl- 加上 -amos。所有規則 -ar 動詞都套用同一組字尾。
explain.en: hablar is a regular -ar verb; the nosotros form is the stem habl- plus -amos. Every regular -ar verb uses the same set of endings.

explain.zh: tener 在 tú 和 él 的形式會有 e → ie 的字根變化：tienes / tiene。但 yo 是完全不規則的 tengo，nosotros 則回到規則的 tenemos。
explain.en: tener has an e → ie stem change in the tú and él forms: tienes / tiene. But yo is the completely irregular tengo, and nosotros returns to the regular tenemos.

explain.zh: somos 已經表明主詞是「我們」，所以 nosotros 通常省略。兩種寫法都對，但母語者多半只說 Somos amigos。
explain.en: somos already identifies the subject as "we", so nosotros is usually dropped. Both versions are correct, but native speakers mostly just say Somos amigos.

prompt.en: We are friends.

explain.zh: 「你們」在拉美是 ustedes，動詞用第三人稱複數 son。絕對不要用 vosotros sois。
explain.en: "You all" is ustedes in Latin America, taking the third-person plural son. Never use vosotros sois.

prompt.en: Are you all from Ecuador?

explain.zh: 這裡兩個代名詞都說出來了，因為句子在做「我 vs 她」的對比 —— 這正是主詞代名詞該出現的時機。
explain.en: Both pronouns appear here because the sentence is drawing a contrast between "I" and "she" — exactly the situation where subject pronouns belong.

prompt.zh: 我來自台灣，而她來自厄瓜多。

explain.en: The Spanish verb form already marks the person, which makes the subject pronoun optional. Adding yo to every sentence makes it sound as if you're constantly emphasising that it's *you*.

options.en: Because a Spanish sentence can't begin with yo

optionExplains.zh: yo 完全沒有不禮貌的問題。

optionExplains.en: Correct. The verb form carries the person; pronouns appear only for emphasis or contrast.

title.zh: ser vs estar：兩個動詞，兩種用途
title.en: ser vs estar: two verbs, two jobs

intro.zh:
西班牙文有兩個動詞都可以翻成「是」，但用途完全不同，而且用錯不只是文法問題 —— 有時候會改變意思。

最簡單的入門判準：

**ser 講「這是什麼」（本質、身分）；estar 講「現在怎麼樣、在哪裡」（狀態、位置）。**

這一課只處理最基本的用法，完整對比會在 A1 再做一次。
intro.en:
Spanish has two verbs that both translate as "to be", but they do completely different jobs — and getting them wrong isn't only a grammar slip, it can change the meaning.

The simplest starting test:

**ser says what something is (essence, identity); estar says how it is right now, or where it is (state, location).**

This lesson covers only the basics; the full contrast comes back at A1.

rule.zh: **ser** 用於身分、職業、國籍、來源 —— 也就是「這個人／東西是什麼」。
rule.en: **ser** covers identity, profession, nationality and origin — in other words, what a person or thing *is*.

rule.zh: **ser** 也用於本質特徵 —— 不太會改變的性質。
rule.en: **ser** also covers inherent qualities — characteristics that don't really change.

rule.zh: **estar** 用於位置 —— 任何東西在哪裡，一律用 estar，沒有例外。
rule.en: **estar** covers location — where anything is, without exception.

examples.es: El libro está en la mesa.

gloss.en: The book is on the table.

note.zh: 即使位置永遠不變，仍然用 estar
note.en: Still estar, even though the location never changes.

rule.zh: **estar** 用於暫時狀態與情緒 —— 現在是這樣，等一下可能就不是了。
rule.en: **estar** covers temporary states and feelings — true now, possibly not in an hour.

note.en: Tired now; not after a rest.

rule.zh: 同一個形容詞配不同動詞，意思會變。這是 ser / estar 最有意思的地方。
rule.en: The same adjective with a different verb changes the meaning. This is the most interesting thing about ser and estar.

gloss.zh: 這湯（現在嚐起來）很好吃。

pitfalls.zh:
最容易犯的錯不是選錯 ser 或 estar，而是**整個動詞漏掉**：

- ✗ Él alto. → ✓ Él **es** alto.
- ✗ Yo cansado. → ✓ Yo **estoy** cansado.
- ✗ El café caliente. → ✓ El café **está** caliente.

> 自我檢查：每個句子都必須有動詞。只有「主詞 + 形容詞」的組合不成立，不管那個形容詞看起來多完整。

選哪一個的判準：

- 描述「這是什麼人、什麼東西」（身分、職業、來源、本質特徵）→ **ser**
- 描述「現在處於什麼狀態」或「在哪裡」→ **estar**

cansado、contento、caliente、frío 這類會變的狀態，幾乎都是 estar。**位置一律 estar**，即使那個位置永遠不會改變：Quito **está** en Ecuador。

同一個形容詞換動詞會改變意思，這是進階但很實用的一組：

- La sopa **es** buena.（這道湯品質好）
- La sopa **está** buena.（這湯現在嚐起來很好吃）
pitfalls.en:
The most common mistake isn't choosing the wrong one between ser and estar — it's **dropping the verb entirely**:

- ✗ Él alto. → ✓ Él **es** alto.
- ✗ Yo cansado. → ✓ Yo **estoy** cansado.
- ✗ El café caliente. → ✓ El café **está** caliente.

> Self-check: every sentence needs a verb. A bare "subject + adjective" is not a sentence, however complete the adjective makes it feel.

How to choose:

- describing **what someone or something is** (identity, profession, origin, inherent qualities) → **ser**
- describing **what state it's in right now**, or **where it is** → **estar**

Changeable states like cansado, contento, caliente and frío are nearly always estar. **Location is always estar**, even when that location never changes: Quito **está** en Ecuador.

Swapping the verb under the same adjective changes the meaning — an advanced but very practical pair:

- La sopa **es** buena. (this soup is good quality)
- La sopa **está** buena. (this soup tastes good right now)

explain.zh: 職業和身分是「你是什麼」，用 ser：Soy estudiante。注意職業前面不加冠詞。
explain.en: Profession and identity are about what you *are*, so they take ser: Soy estudiante. Note that no article goes before the profession.

prompt.en: Which verb does "I am a student" need?

optionExplains.zh: estar 不用於職業或身分。
optionExplains.en: estar isn't used for professions or identity.

optionExplains.zh: 正確。職業、身分用 ser。
optionExplains.en: Correct. Profession and identity take ser.

optionExplains.zh: 漏了動詞 —— 只有主詞加名詞不成句。

optionExplains.zh: hay 表示存在，不能拿來說自己的身分。

optionExplains.zh: 正確。cansado 是暫時狀態，用 estar。
optionExplains.en: Correct. cansado is a temporary state, so estar.

optionExplains.zh: 漏了動詞，每個句子都必須有動詞。
optionExplains.en: The verb is missing; every sentence needs one.

optionExplains.en: tener means "to have" and doesn't work here.

explain.zh: 「暫時 vs 永久」是入門的簡化說法，但位置是例外 —— **所有位置一律用 estar**，即使是永遠不會移動的城市和山。Quito está en Ecuador。
explain.en: "Temporary versus permanent" is a useful beginner shortcut, but location is the exception — **all locations take estar**, including cities and mountains that never move. Quito está en Ecuador.

prompt.zh: 「基多在厄瓜多。」為什麼用 estar，位置不是永遠不會變嗎？
prompt.en: "Quito is in Ecuador" uses estar. Isn't a location permanent?

options.zh: 因為位置一律用 estar，不管會不會改變

因為 Quito 是專有名詞

optionExplains.zh: 當然不會移動。
optionExplains.en: It certainly doesn't move.

optionExplains.zh: 正確。位置是 estar 的絕對領域，不看「會不會變」這個標準。
optionExplains.en: Correct. Location is estar's absolute territory, regardless of whether it changes.

optionExplains.zh: Quito es en Ecuador 是錯的。
optionExplains.en: Quito es en Ecuador is wrong.

optionExplains.zh: 跟專有名詞無關。

explain.zh: 同一個形容詞配不同動詞會改變意思。La sopa es buena 是對這道湯的品質評價；La sopa está buena 是「現在吃起來很好吃」。這種對比在 A1 會更深入。
explain.en: The same adjective with a different verb changes the meaning. La sopa es buena judges the soup's quality; La sopa está buena says it tastes good right now. This contrast is explored further at A1.

prompt.zh: La sopa es buena 和 La sopa está buena 差在哪裡？
prompt.en: What's the difference between La sopa es buena and La sopa está buena?

options.zh: es buena 是說湯本身品質好；está buena 是說現在嚐起來很好吃
options.en: es buena judges the soup's quality; está buena says it tastes good right now

options.zh: es buena 用於書面，está buena 用於口語
options.en: es buena is written and está buena is spoken

optionExplains.zh: 兩句意思確實不同。
optionExplains.en: The two do mean different things.

optionExplains.zh: 正確。ser 講本質評價，estar 講當下的狀態或感受。
optionExplains.en: Correct. ser judges an inherent quality; estar describes the current state or impression.

optionExplains.zh: 兩句都合乎文法。
optionExplains.en: Both are grammatical.

optionExplains.zh: 差別在意思，不在語體。
optionExplains.en: The difference is in meaning, not in register.

explain.zh: estar 的第一人稱是 estoy。注意 tú 以下的形式都有重音符號：estás / está / están，只有 estamos 沒有。
explain.en: The first-person form of estar is estoy. Note that every form from tú onwards carries an accent — estás / está / están — with only estamos going without.

explain.zh: está 的重音符號不能省 —— esta（沒符號）是「這個」的意思，是完全不同的字。
explain.en: The accent on está can't be dropped: esta without it means "this", a completely different word.

explain.zh: 身高是本質特徵，所以用 ser 不是 estar。動詞 es 不能省 —— 只有主詞加形容詞不成句。
explain.en: Height is an inherent characteristic, so it takes ser rather than estar. The verb es is required — a subject and adjective alone don't make a sentence.

prompt.en: My brother is tall.

explain.zh: 這一句要同時做對三件事：冠詞 el、動詞 está，以及選 estar 而非 ser（溫度是會變的狀態）。
explain.en: Three things have to be right in this one sentence: the article el, the verb está, and choosing estar over ser (temperature is a changeable state).

prompt.en: The coffee is hot.

explain.zh: 位置用 estar。疑問詞 dónde 放句首並帶重音符號，動詞緊接在後，主詞放最後。
explain.en: Location takes estar. The question word dónde goes first and carries an accent, the verb follows immediately, and the subject comes last.

prompt.en: Where is the bathroom?

explain.zh: El niño alto 只有「主詞 + 形容詞」，缺了動詞，正確是 El niño **es** alto。這是這一課最重要的自我檢查點。
explain.en: El niño alto is only a subject plus an adjective, with no verb; the correct form is El niño **es** alto. That's the most important self-check in this lesson.

prompt.zh: 下列哪一句漏掉了動詞？
prompt.en: Which sentence is missing its verb?

optionExplains.zh: 有動詞 está。
optionExplains.en: It has the verb está.

optionExplains.zh: 有動詞 es。
optionExplains.en: It has the verb es.

optionExplains.zh: 正確找到錯誤。應該是 El niño es alto。
optionExplains.en: Correct. It should be El niño es alto.

optionExplains.zh: 有動詞 estoy。
optionExplains.en: It has the verb estoy.

intro.zh:
最後一課給你一個極度好用的字：**hay**。

它表示「存在」，而且是 A0 階段最不用動腦的一個字 —— **不分單複數、不分陰陽性、永遠就是 hay 這三個字母。**

要小心的只有一件事：hay 和 tener 的分工。兩者都可以翻成「有」，用法卻完全不同。
intro.en:
The last lesson gives you an extremely useful word: **hay**.

It means "there is" or "there are", and it's the least demanding word you'll meet at A0 — **no singular/plural, no gender, always just those three letters.**

There's only one thing to watch: how hay divides the work with tener.

rule.zh: hay 表示某處存在某物，單數複數都用同一個形式，永遠不變。
rule.en: hay says that something exists somewhere. The form is identical for singular and plural and never changes.

examples.es: Hay un mercado en esta calle.

gloss.en: There's a market on this street.

note.en: Negate by putting no in front.

rule.zh: hay 後面接**不定冠詞或數字，或什麼都不接**，但**不接定冠詞**。這是最常見的錯誤來源。
rule.en: hay is followed by **an indefinite article, a number, or nothing at all** — but **never a definite article**. This is the most common source of errors.

examples.es: Hay un libro en la mesa.

gloss.en: There's a book on the table.
There are books on the table.

rule.zh: **hay 講「存在」，estar 講「位置」。** 東西第一次出現用 hay，已知的東西講它在哪裡用 estar。
rule.en: **hay is about existence; estar is about location.** Use hay when something first comes up, and estar to say where a known thing is.

examples.es: Hay un banco en la calle.

gloss.en: There's a bank on the street.

note.zh: 第一次提到，聽者還不知道
note.en: First mention — the listener doesn't know about it yet.

examples.es: El banco está en la calle.

gloss.en: The bank is on the street.

note.zh: 雙方都知道是哪家銀行

rule.zh: **hay 講「存在」，tener 講「擁有」。** 中文都說「有」，西班牙文分得很清楚。
rule.en: **hay is about existence; tener is about possession.** The two cannot be swapped.

examples.es: Hay dos hermanos en la casa.

gloss.en: There are two brothers in the house.

pitfalls.zh:
**hay 表示「存在」，tener 表示「擁有」，兩者不能互換。**

- ✓ **Hay** dos hermanos en la casa.（某處存在兩個兄弟）
- ✓ **Tengo** dos hermanos.（我擁有／我的親屬關係）

造句前先確認：這是「某處存在某物」還是「某人擁有某物」？

**第二個坑：hay 後面不接定冠詞。**

- ✓ Hay **un** libro en la mesa.
- ✓ Hay libros en la mesa.
- ✗ Hay **el** libro en la mesa.

原因很直觀：hay 是用來介紹聽者還不知道的新東西，而定冠詞 el 表示「雙方都知道是哪一個」，兩者邏輯上互相衝突。要講已知的東西在哪裡，改用 estar：El libro **está** en la mesa。

> hay 和 estar 的分工：問存不存在用 **hay**（¿Hay un baño aquí?），已知它存在、要問在哪裡用 **estar**（¿Dónde está el baño?）。

**好消息：hay 完全不變化。** 不分單複數、不分性別、不隨人稱變 —— 一家餐廳是 hay，三家餐廳還是 hay。
pitfalls.en:
**hay says something exists; tener says someone owns it. They are not interchangeable.**

- ✓ **Hay** dos hermanos en la casa. (two brothers exist somewhere)
- ✓ **Tengo** dos hermanos. (I have them — a family relationship)

Before building a sentence, check: is this "something exists somewhere" or "someone possesses something"?

**Second pitfall: hay is not followed by a definite article.**

- ✓ Hay **un** libro en la mesa.
- ✓ Hay libros en la mesa.
- ✗ Hay **el** libro en la mesa.

The reason is intuitive: hay introduces something the listener doesn't know about yet, while the definite article el says "we both know which one" — the two contradict each other. To say where a known thing is, switch to estar: El libro **está** en la mesa.

> How hay and estar divide the work: ask whether something exists with **hay** (¿Hay un baño aquí?), and ask where a known thing is with **estar** (¿Dónde está el baño?).

**The good news: hay never changes.** No singular or plural, no gender, no person — one restaurant is hay, and three restaurants is still hay.

explain.zh: hay 永遠是 hay —— 一家是 hay，三家也是 hay。這是它最好用的地方。
explain.en: hay is always hay — one restaurant is hay, three restaurants is still hay. That's what makes it so easy to use.

prompt.en: How do you say "there are three restaurants here"?

optionExplains.zh: 正確。hay 不分單複數，三家餐廳也是 hay。
optionExplains.en: Correct. hay doesn't change for number; three restaurants is still hay.

optionExplains.zh: hay 永遠不變形，沒有複數形式。
optionExplains.en: hay never inflects and has no plural form.

optionExplains.zh: estar 講已知東西的位置，不用來介紹新事物的存在。
optionExplains.en: estar states where a known thing is; it doesn't introduce something new.

optionExplains.zh: tener 是「擁有」，主詞會變成「他們擁有三家餐廳」。
optionExplains.en: tener means "to have", making the subject "they own three restaurants".

explain.zh: hay 是用來介紹「新的、聽者還不知道」的東西，定冠詞 el 卻表示「雙方都知道是哪一個」，兩者互相矛盾。要講已知的書在哪，用 El libro está en la mesa。
explain.en: hay introduces something the listener doesn't yet know about, while the definite article el says "we both know which one" — the two contradict each other. To say where a known book is, use El libro está en la mesa.

prompt.en: Which sentence is wrong?

options.zh: Hay un libro en la mesa.
options.en: Hay un libro en la mesa.

options.zh: Hay el libro en la mesa.
options.en: Hay el libro en la mesa.

options.zh: El libro está en la mesa.
options.en: El libro está en la mesa.

optionExplains.zh: hay + 不定冠詞，正確。
optionExplains.en: hay + indefinite article — correct.

optionExplains.zh: hay + 無冠詞複數，正確。
optionExplains.en: hay + a bare plural — correct.

optionExplains.zh: 正確找到錯誤。hay 後面不能接定冠詞 el。
optionExplains.en: Correct. hay can't be followed by the definite article el.

optionExplains.zh: 已知的書講位置用 estar，正確。
optionExplains.en: A known book's location uses estar — correct.

explain.zh: hay 講「某處存在某物」，tener 講「某人擁有某物」。「我有兩個兄弟」是擁有 → Tengo dos hermanos。
explain.en: hay states that something exists somewhere; tener states that someone possesses it. "I have two brothers" is possession → Tengo dos hermanos.

prompt.zh: 「我有兩個兄弟」該用 hay 還是 tener？
prompt.en: Should "I have two brothers" use hay or tener?

optionExplains.zh: 這句意思會變成「（某處）有兩個兄弟」，沒有說是誰的。
optionExplains.en: That would mean "there are two brothers (somewhere)", without saying whose.

optionExplains.zh: 正確。「我擁有」用 tener。
optionExplains.en: Correct. Possession takes tener.

optionExplains.zh: estar 不表示擁有。
optionExplains.en: estar doesn't express possession.

optionExplains.zh: 文法不通。
optionExplains.en: Not grammatical.

explain.zh: ¿Hay un baño aquí? 問的是「存不存在」；¿Dónde está el baño? 預設有，直接問位置。實務上兩句都很常用，在餐廳直接問後者，在路上問前者比較自然。
explain.en: ¿Hay un baño aquí? asks whether one exists; ¿Dónde está el baño? assumes there is one and asks where. Both are common in practice — in a restaurant ask the second, on the street the first feels more natural.

prompt.zh: 你在陌生的地方想找洗手間，第一句該問什麼？
prompt.en: You're somewhere unfamiliar and want to find a bathroom. What do you ask first?

options.zh: 兩個前者都可以，但意思略有不同
options.en: Either of the first two, with a slight difference in meaning

optionExplains.zh: 這句預設「這裡一定有洗手間」，直接問位置。
optionExplains.en: This assumes there is definitely one here and goes straight to location.

optionExplains.zh: 這句是問「這裡有沒有」，還不確定存在。
optionExplains.en: This asks whether one exists at all.

optionExplains.zh: 這是問對方「您有沒有洗手間」，語感怪。
optionExplains.en: This asks the person whether *they* have a bathroom, which sounds odd.

optionExplains.zh: 正確。兩句都能用，差別在你是否已經確定這裡有洗手間。
optionExplains.en: Correct. Both work; the difference is whether you already know one exists.

explain.zh: 否定就是在 hay 前面加 no。這句是日常最常聽到的固定說法之一。
explain.en: Negate simply by putting no in front of hay. This is one of the most frequently heard set phrases in everyday speech.

prompt.en: No problem.

explain.zh: 第一次提到這個市場，所以用 hay + 不定冠詞 un。如果對方已經知道是哪個市場，才會說 El mercado está en esta calle。
explain.en: The market is being mentioned for the first time, so hay + the indefinite article un. If the listener already knows which market, you'd say El mercado está en esta calle instead.

prompt.en: There's a market on this street.

accept: Hay un mercado en esta calle
hay un mercado en esta calle

explain.zh: hay + 數字 + 複數名詞。注意 hay 本身不變複數，但 silla 要變成 sillas。
explain.en: hay + a number + a plural noun. Note that hay itself doesn't become plural, but silla has to become sillas.

prompt.en: There are four chairs in the kitchen.

explain.zh: baño 的 ñ 唸成接近「尼」的音，aquí 的重音在最後一個音節。這是旅途上最實用的句子之一。
explain.en: The ñ in baño sounds like the ny in canyon, and aquí is stressed on the last syllable. This is one of the most useful sentences on any trip.

explain.zh: hay 是 haber 的無人稱形式，永遠不變。學到這裡你已經看過 ser 和 estar 各有五種變化，hay 只有一種 —— 好好享受。
explain.en: hay is the impersonal form of haber and never changes. By now you've seen ser and estar with five forms each; hay has exactly one — enjoy it.

prompt.en: How many forms does hay have?

options.zh: 兩種：單數 hay、複數 han
options.en: Two: singular hay and plural han

options.zh: 五種，跟其他動詞一樣有五個人稱
options.en: Five, one per person like other verbs

options.zh: 兩種：陽性 hay、陰性 haya
options.en: Two: masculine hay and feminine haya

optionExplains.zh: hay 沒有複數形式。
optionExplains.en: hay has no plural form.

optionExplains.zh: 正確。不分單複數、不分性別、不隨人稱變化。
optionExplains.en: Correct. No number, no gender, no person.

optionExplains.zh: hay 是無人稱形式，不隨人稱變。
optionExplains.en: hay is impersonal and doesn't inflect for person.

optionExplains.zh: hay 不隨性別變化。
optionExplains.en: hay doesn't inflect for gender.
